title: Utility Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. — Order No. U-35523 accepts the Joint Report filed into the record on October 9, 2026, thereby recognizing ELL’s compliance with the FAC General Order for the audit period, subject to certain conditions. The vote occurred at the Commission’s October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                 ORDER NUMBER U-35523

              LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION, EX PARTE.

Docket No. U-35523, In re: Audit of Fuel Adjustment Clause Filings for Entergy Louisiana,
LLC for the period of January 2016 through December 2019. (This matter was originally
published as X-35523, and is being republished to provide notice of the issuance of Staff’s Audit
Report and to allow for intervention and/or comments).

              (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                            ORDER

OVERVIEW

       This Commission, having reviewed and considered the Joint Report on Staff’s Audit Report

of Fuel Adjustment Clause Filings for Entergy Louisiana, LLC for the Period of January 2016

through December 2019 (the “Joint Report”) submitted by Entergy Louisiana, LLC (“ELL”) and

Louisiana Public Service Commission Staff (“LPSC Staff”), finds said Joint Report to be

acceptable and in accordance with the provisions of the Commission’s General Order in Docket

No. U-21497, dated November 6, 1997. The Joint Report indicated that ELL complied with the

General Order dated November 6, 1997 specifying includable and excludable Fuel Adjustment

Clause (“FAC”) costs. The Joint Report also included the following recommendations from the

Sierra Club, which were unopposed by ELL: which were unopposed by ELL:

       1.      For the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (“MISO”) Day Ahead
       market, Nelson 6’s offer commitment status will be changed to a default
       “economic’ offer commitment status and will include start up or no-load costs.
       Nelson 6 offers into the MISO Day Ahead market will be cost-based; however,
       Nelson 6 may be offered as Must Run under the following circumstances:
       a.      To avoid cycling during time periods where Nelson 6 is required for
       increased reliability
       b.      When the cost associated with not fulfilling contractual obligations (ex.
       fuel/transportation contracts) exceeds the operating cost of the unit
       2.      To determine determining O&M costs for the purposes of making offers
       into the MISO Day Ahead Market for Nelson 6, Entergy will use three distinct
       components.
       a.      The operating fuel usage/cost is represented by the input/output
       (MMBtu/hr) curve derived from Nelson 6’s Heat Rate test. Fleet engineers monitor
       heat rate monthly to ensure accurate fuel costs are being utilized and deviations are
       addressed. In future fuel adjustment clause proceedings covering audit periods
       commencing after Commission approval of this settlement agreement (i.e., 2024
       and beyond), Entergy will be prepared to provide to the Commission and any
       intervenors information as to how the fuel costs are calculated and where the fuel
       costs are coming from (e.g., spot market costs, fuel inventory costs) and what costs
       are included (e.g., mine mouth, transportation).
       b.      The operating non-fuel costs are represented as No-Load O&M ($/hr) and
       variable O&M ($/MWh) adders. The total O&M is calculated by averaging together
       the production-related variable costs from the unit’s 4-year historical spend. The
       annual average total cost is split between No-Load, Variable O&M, and non-fuel
       start-up costs.. Costs allocated to No-load O&M are divided by the unit’s annual

                                                                               Order No. U-35523
                                                                                          Page 1
        average service hours. Costs allocated to variable O&M are divided by the unit’s
       annual average generation production (MWh). Costs allocated to non-fuel start up
       are divided by the unit’s average annual starts. These O&M calculations are
       updated annually and benchmarked with industry studies. In future fuel adjustment
       clause proceedings covering audit periods commencing after Commission approval
       of this settlement agreement (i.e., 2024 and beyond), Entergy will be prepared to
       provide to the Commission and any intervenors with the analysis it conducts to
       calculate the total O&M, including the historical and forecasted spending data that
       feeds into the calculations. Entergy will also provide to the Commission the
       benchmarking analysis and industry data that it uses to benchmark its O&M
       calculations.
       3.      The Company will utilize projected market revenues to make commitment
       decisions. The Company has designated systems to assist in the analysis of
       expected market revenues and the forecasting process is continuously refined. In
       future fuel adjustment clause proceedings covering audit periods commencing after
       Commission approval of this settlement agreement (i.e., 2024 and beyond), Entergy
       will be prepared to provide the Commission and any intervenors a summary of how
       its projected revenues compared to actual market prices and revenues, and explain
       what actions the Company took to respond to deviations.
       4.      The Company agrees to document instances in which Nelson 6’s
       commitment status is determined to be must run. The basis for changes in
       commitment status from Economic to Must Run will be noted in the Company’s
       MISO Market Software.


COMMISSION JURISDICTION

       The Commission exercises jurisdiction over public utilities in Louisiana pursuant to

Article IV, Section 21 of the Louisiana Constitution, which states:

       La. Const. Art. IV, Sec. 21 provides in pertinent part:
       The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public utilities and have
       such other regulatory authority as provided by law. It shall adopt and enforce
       reasonable rules, regulations, and procedures necessary for the discharge of its
       duties, and shall have other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.

       Pursuant to that exercise of jurisdiction, the Commission issued General Order dated

November 6, 1997, establishing a FAC whereby jurisdictional electric utilities may pass through

to customers certain costs associated with fuel and purchased power.



COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

       This matter was considered at the Commission’s October 22, 2026, Business and Executive

Session. On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and unanimously

adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Joint Report filed into the record on October 9, 2026.




                                                                              Order No. U-35523
                                                                                         Page 2
 IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       The Joint Report submitted on October 9, 2026 is accepted.

This Order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
November 19, 2026
